the preparation of Er(3+): ZBYA glass, the spectroscopic properties, and the potential application in 2.8 μm laser materials.
the synthesis and characterization of Er(3+), Tm(3+) and Yb(3+)/Er(3+) co-doped ZrF₄-based fluoride glasses.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Er(3+): ZrF(3+)-based glass is a promising candidate for 2.8 μm laser materials.
the ZrF4- based glasses are very promising candidates for 2.70 μm laser materials.
the new ZrF(3+)-based glass is a promising candidate for the 2.7μm laser material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ZrF(3+) ion can replace YF(3+) in ZBLA-type glass and it is a good candidate to replace the BaF(2) in ZBLAN-type glass, because the ZrF3+ ion can form a stable glass network and it can also enhance the thermal properties of the glass.
the Er(3+):ZBYA glass is an excellent 2.7-μm laser material.
the new ZrF(2)-BaF(2)-Y(2)O(3)-AlF(3)-NaF (ZBYA) glasses have the potential to become an important candidate in the development of 2.7-μm fiber amplifiers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ZrF4 based glasses are a good alternative to the ZBLAN system for 2.6-2.8 μm emission, with the advantage of a much higher Er concentration and a lower cost.
the ZrF(3+)-based glasses can provide a new platform for the development of high-performance 2.7μm laser materials.
the Er(3+):ZBYA glass is a promising laser material for 2.71 μm laser applications.
